method: Recomputed from the recipes alone (theories/*.json keys experiment, recipe, unit, refuted_by) before opening tests/; scripts r4-m10_p*.py, r4-m01_p*.py, r4-m10_capcounts.py, common.py; row files fetched to runs/replication/ (not committed). Bootstrap: 2,000 resamples, seed 0, percentile 90 %.

predictions.recipe_summary: Cap-hit fraction, RL step 100 minus base, plain MATH-500, T 0.6/top-p 0.95, sample 0, first row per problem_index, paired on the common set.
predictions.note: Both files hold all 500 problems at sample 0, so paired and unpaired readings coincide. Paired bootstrap over 500 problems, 2,000 resamples, seed 0.

predictions.recipe_summary: Cap-hit fraction, RL step 400 minus base, plain MATH-500, T 0.6/top-p 0.95, paired.
predictions.note: Same seeds and prompts as base (seed and prompt_n_tokens equal on 500/500).

predictions.recipe_summary: Cap-hit fraction, RL step 400 minus base, plain, clean harder 328, T 0.6/top-p 0.95, paired.
predictions.ambiguity: The clean list (sets.hard.flags) is keyed by hard.json index, not unique_id; the recipe's file path 'results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json' is relative to studies/rlneurons. Literal: map index -> unique_id via studies/rlneurons/data/rln3/hard.json and match rows by unique_id. Alternative: match by problem_index == int(key).
predictions.note: Both readings select the same 328 problems. Base 137 cap hits equals studies/rlneurons/README.md line 160.

predictions.recipe_summary: Share of step-400 cap hits (plain MATH-500, T 0.6/top-p 0.95, sample 0) that are rule-A loops (any 8,000-char window starting at a line start with zlib default ratio < 0.10).
predictions.ambiguity: none in the recipe; it restates rln4_lib.onset_lines' window test exactly (onset_lines is not None iff a window passes). Alternative computed: rln3's stored loop_ratio field < 0.10.
predictions.note: All 98 cap hits are >= 8,000 characters. The 20 non-loop cap hits have minimum window ratios 0.102-0.27, 16 of them below 0.17: the 0.10 threshold cuts through a continuum of repetition, so the share moves with the threshold (about 0.87 at 0.12). Bootstrap over the 98 cap-hit rows.

predictions.recipe_summary: AUROC of -zlib9 ratio of text[:6000] for stored loop_A, base cue MATH-500 T 0.6/top-p 1.0 (d4fa), rows >= 6,000 chars, loops with onset_A_char < 7,000 or missing dropped.
predictions.note: 500 rows, 71 loop_A true (README line 131 says 71), 20 dropped for early onset. Bootstrap over kept rows.

predictions.recipe_summary: Share of problems where base-cue (F_math500) text[:3000] compresses better (zlib 9) than RL step 2,800 plain text[:3000], sample 0, both >= 3,000 chars; ties 0.5.
predictions.ambiguity: none found; no duplicate sample-0 rows. Both texts begin with ' line!\n\nOkay' (base: the prefilled cue is in text; RL writes it itself), so the openings are comparable.
predictions.note: Kept pairs are problems where both models wrote >= 3,000 characters (311 of 500). Bootstrap over pairs.

predictions.recipe_summary: Mean over K_own and K_rl of the per-file AUROC of -zlib9 ratio of stored text[:3000] for cap_hit; rows >= 3,000 chars; loops with onset_A_char < 4,000 or missing dropped.
predictions.ambiguity: The recipe says to use stored text as it is; stored text = cue + given prefix + continuation (K_own text shares a median 6,568 leading characters with base-01's F answer), so text[:3000] is mostly the prefix the model was handed, not text it generated. Literal reading followed; a generated-only reading needs the tokenizer to cut at n_prefix and was not computed.
predictions.note: Bootstrap resamples each file's rows independently (seed 0). The 90 % interval of the mean includes 0.5, and so does each per-file interval: the AUROC is not established above chance even though it clears the 0.53 refutation bar.

a_cap_hit_counts_plain_T0.6_topp0.95_sam.rerun_spread_in_README: studies/rlneurons/README.md lines 101-102: base plain T 0.6 cap hits 65 (RLN-3 base-01) vs 69 (n13 run, same seeds per inventory); lines 103-107 vs my count: RL plain T 0.6 19 (s2800-01) vs 16 (n13 run, line 106); line 252: T1/T2 reruns on their seeds 25 vs 27 and 6 vs 6 cap hits of 500; line 189: 2 vs 4 of 50. Run-to-run spread is 0-4 cap hits of 500.
a_cap_hit_counts_plain_T0.6_topp0.95_sam.rise_vs_spread: base -> step 100 is +38 (65 -> 103), base -> step 400 +33 (65 -> 98) on MATH-500, and +23 (137 -> 160) on the clean 328; about 8-10x the 0-4 rerun spread. Paired 90 % intervals exclude 0 (p1, p2, p3). Paired detail: 68 problems cap only at step 100, 30 only at base.
a_cap_hit_counts_plain_T0.6_topp0.95_sam.caveat: Steps 100 and 400 ran in one later job on another instance (r3/s0400_s0100-01), the base in base-01; same seeds and prompts. Steps 100/400 do not write the cue (0/500 texts start with ' line!'), step 2,800 does (495/500).

b_already_in_git.answer: No for steps 100 and 400. Yes for the endpoints.
b_already_in_git.detail: No committed file or pre-cutoff board item (before.jsonl) holds a step-100 or step-400 cap-hit count; studies/rlneurons/README.md line 1140 says the step-400 rows are not scored, and results/ has no s0100/s0400 readout (only offline_gate.json, a stand-in run with no cap-hit counts). The endpoints were in the README: base 65 of 500 (line 101), base 137 and RL 64 of 328 (lines 160, 162), RL n13 16 of 500 (line 106). The theory also cites knowledge-b15a21 (RL-Zero-Math 3.0: 29.1 % vs 17.8 % length-limit hits at T 0.6), which points to the direction of the rise. So the middle numbers were not sitting in a table; the endpoint direction 'step 2,800 far below base' was.

step6.loop_row: step 400, problem 9, cap hit, 69,780 chars, rule-A loop from char 7,502: ends mid-sentence in a verbatim-repeated paragraph about parenthesizations of 2*3*4*5+1 ('...But the example shows that by grouping'); a 200-char tail fragment recurs 47 times; last-8,000 ratio 0.069.
step6.nonloop_row: step 400, problem 11, cap hit, 46,867 chars, not a loop (min window ratio 0.17): ends mid-sentence restating the same polynomial argument p(n) = k(n-2)...(n-7) + 1/(2(n-1)) + ...; a 200-char tail fragment recurs 10 times, so it is looser repetition, not new reasoning.
step6.judgement: The loop flag means verbatim block repetition as the theory says; but 16 of the 20 non-loop cap hits sit just above the 0.10 threshold (0.102-0.17) and also repeat, so 'non-loop' here is not 'long productive reasoning'.
